title: Token latency trace-correlation & circuit surface mapping for multi-region failover
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: Build end-to-end instrumentation and dashboards that correlate per-token latency breakdowns with circuit state and region failover surface area. This ticket covers: 1) adding token-granular timing spans along the admission -> dispatch -> decode path with consistent trace IDs and exemplars, 2) exposing circuit manager surface metrics (circuit_state, open_duration, trip_count) with region/shard/model_version tags, 3) aggregating per-token histograms and percentile rollups (p50/p95/p99) with key dimensions for multi-region SLO alignment, and 4) a runbook + alerting policy for region failover and load-shedding scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Per-token timing spans instrumented and exported via OTLP with exemplars on key metrics (admit_wait_ms, dispatch_ms, decode_token_ms, kv_cache_hit) in prod canary and at 1% synthetic traffic.
Circuit surface metrics published: circuit_state{region,shard,model_version}, circuit_open_count, circuit_open_duration_seconds, with labels consistent across control-plane and agent instrumentation.

Grafana dashboard created with panels: (a) token-level waterfall decomposed by stage, (b) histogram heatmap of token decode p95/p99 per region, (c) circuit state timeline and open_count overlays, (d) KV cache hit-rate correlation panel, (e) SLO burn-rate & alerting widget.
Runbook captured in Confluence with step-by-step failover procedures, correlation playbook for diagnosing high p99 tokens, and automated remediation triggers documented.

SLO test: synthetic traffic test demonstrates correct failover when a region's admission drops below 25% admit rate for 5 minutes; metrics show circuits opening and traffic shifting to fallback region without violating customer-visible latency SLO in downstream sample apps.
PRs merged for instrumentation and dashboard JSON exported to dashboards repo; deployment includes feature flag gating for rollout.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Initial design sync: agreed to use OTLP traces + metric exemplars to avoid separate correlation glue. Action items: add exemplar support on admit meter (Chris), update agent lib to attach traceID to token-level spans (Liam).

2026-02-19 - Spike results: microbench shows adding per-token span with lightweight annotations increases hot-path p50 by ~1.8ms and p99 by ~2.3ms when sampling all tokens. Decision: sample 1% full-span traces in steady-state, 100% for synthetic test mode. Recorded in design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Token+Trace+Correlation
2026-02-25 - PR #8271 opened for agent tracing hooks (github.com/redwood-inference/agent/pull/8271). Waiting on Security review for trace sampling config.

2026-03-01 - Architecture review with SRE: recommended storing histograms using HDR buckets at ingestion to reduce cardinality and avoid raw per-token indexing. Trade-off: lose some precision on tail but gain 8x lower storage. Added metric: token_histogram_exemplar_count to capture a few raw exemplars per minute.
2026-03-05 - Dashboard draft created in grafana (UID: DkRkt7). Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/DkRkt7/token-latency-circuit-surface. Shared with PM and reliability guild for feedback.

2026-03-09 - Review feedback from PM (Sofia Patel): request to add customer-impact tagging (customer_id) on sampled traces for top 1% of offending requests. Liam: will add opt-in PII-safe mapping and only attach hashed customer_id on opt-in customers.

2026-03-10 - Blocker: need schema change approved for circuit_state metric labels (region, shard, model_version) to maintain uniformity across services. Filing ENG-1004520 to approve metric naming convention and export contract.
notes: Implementation decisions: use HDR histograms + exemplars, 1% trace sampling in prod, full tracing in synthetic harness. For dashboards, use rollup queries to prometheus-like store (telescope) with region and model_version dims. We'll also add a lightweight admission counter metric (admit_result{ok|rejected|shed}) to drive SLOs and burn-rate calculations.
